Predict risk of death with ADT alone or with an ARPI plus ADT

Source: R/predict.R
predict_risk.Rd

Adds each patient's linear predictor and predicted risk of death within 4 years with androgen deprivation therapy (ADT) alone, called baseline risk, with an androgen receptor pathway inhibitor (ARPI) plus ADT, or both.

Usage

predict_risk(newdata, treatment = c("adt", "arpi"), model = mhspc_model())

Arguments

newdata

A data frame with one row per patient and one column per input listed by model_inputs(): ecog_ps (0, 1, or 2), gleason_score (2 to 10), visceral_metastasis (0 or 1, or logical), bone_metastases (a count, or a category code "0-3", "4-6", "7-10", or "11+"), psa (ng/mL), hemoglobin (g/L), albumin (g/L), alp (U/L), and ldh (U/L). Other columns are kept unchanged.

treatment

Treatments to predict risk for: "adt", ADT alone, and "arpi", an ARPI plus ADT.

model

An mhspc_model object from mhspc_model().

Value

newdata with linear_predictor, the model's risk score, and, for each treatment in the order requested, the predicted 4-year risk of death as a proportion: baseline_risk for ADT alone and arpi_risk for an ARPI plus ADT. Existing columns with these names are replaced.

Details

The risk with an ARPI plus ADT is the baseline risk minus the absolute risk difference at that baseline risk, the ard estimate of estimate_treatment_effect(). It therefore reflects how the treatment effect varies with baseline risk, not a constant hazard ratio. For baseline risks outside the range in which effects were estimated, the effect at the nearest edge of that range is used, with a warning.

Inputs are checked first. Missing or invalid values stop with an error that names the row and input. Values outside the range in the trial data give a warning, because their estimates are extrapolations. Values above the upper cap used in model development are scored at the cap, with a message.

Examples

# Your own patient data: one row per patient, one column per input, plus any
# other columns, which are kept.
patients <- data.frame(
  patient_id = c("A", "B"),
  ecog_ps = c(0, 1), gleason_score = c(9, 9), visceral_metastasis = c(0, 0),
  bone_metastases = c(8, 15), psa = c(45, 150), hemoglobin = c(128, 115),
  albumin = c(41, 38), alp = c(180, 420), ldh = c(210, 280)
)

# Risk with ADT alone and with an ARPI plus ADT
risk <- predict_risk(patients)
risk[c("patient_id", "baseline_risk", "arpi_risk")]
#>   patient_id baseline_risk arpi_risk
#> 1          A     0.6160547 0.4595782
#> 2          B     0.8956950 0.7680623

# Risk with ADT alone only
predict_risk(patients, treatment = "adt")
#>   patient_id ecog_ps gleason_score visceral_metastasis bone_metastases psa
#> 1          A       0             9                   0               8  45
#> 2          B       1             9                   0              15 150
#>   hemoglobin albumin alp ldh linear_predictor baseline_risk
#> 1        128      41 180 210        0.8187273     0.6160547
#> 2        115      38 420 280        1.6781886     0.8956950
